_about: App-only recommendation extras. Seven Pens' ratings, notes and lists, and prices, live in DrawTabData (data/recommendations, data/prices; see its docs/RECOMMENDATIONS.md and docs/PRICES.md). What stays here isn't a DrawTabData entity yet: FamilyRecs (product lines such as iPads and Galaxy Tabs, matched to tablets by MemberPrefix or Members), AlsoSoldAs names, and RatingAliases for labels renamed since (DECENT became OK on 2026-11-13).

AlsoSoldAs.Note: Original SKU with more accessories. Same tablet.

Notes.Text: iPads play the role of a drawing tablet very well, and they are great general-purpose tablets.
The Apple Pencil does not come with an iPad. Budget for buying it separately.
The S Pen comes in the box, which keeps the cost down.
Samsung provides Android updates for 7 years, the best of any Android tablet brand.
The S Pen has a high initial activation force, so drawing is basic. Better for notes, whiteboarding and general use.
Lots of models that vary in size and cost.
They use a USI pen instead of EMR. Reviewers found problems with the pen, including severe diagonal wobble. Seven has not tried them.
A laptop that folds over. The drawing experience is good, not great.
Comes with an S Pen. Many people use the Wacom CP-913 pen with it instead.
The drawing experience is OK. Better suited to note-taking and whiteboarding than drawing.
No pen in the box. The Surface Slim Pen 2 is sold separately.

FamilyRecs.Name: Pen computers (Wacom MobileStudio Pro, Huion Kamvas Studio)

Notes.Text: Seven does not recommend pen computers: high purchase, support and repair costs, and no upgradability.
Some people love them. See the alternatives to pen computers in the docs before you buy one.
